clue.text: Token clue

definitions.meaning: a token is an outward mark or indication of something
a clue is a hint or indication pointing to something

explanation.definitionFit: Both a token and a clue are indications: a gesture given as a token, and a telltale hint pointing the way.

clue.text: Bitter about the north? You may be this!

definitions.text: Bitter about the north? You may be this!

parts.words: Bitter about the north? You may be this!
parts.note: someone resentful of the north of England is likely to hail from the other end of the country

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like the beer, and the clue reads as a dig at regional rivalry: the person sniping at the north presumably comes from the opposite half of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of the lower half of England is described by the adjective for that region, opposite the north.

clue.text: Golf setter played when putting in America, most impressive

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: putting in says the letter for America is placed inside the reworked setter
played suggests the letters of setter are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A golfer who sets puzzles plays a round in America, with impressive putting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' turns SETTER into RETEST, and 'putting in' puts A inside it to give REATEST after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of great: the most impressive of all is the greatest.

clue.text: Mad character in following chapter originally goes rabbiting

indicators.note: following says the character and in come after the chapter abbreviation

parts.note: the Mad Hatter is a character in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
taken as written

indicators.note: originally means at the outset, so only the opening letter of goes is taken

explanation.surface: In the next chapter of the novel, a crazy character starts talking nonsense at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like an anagram signal, but it names the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland. 'originally' applies only to 'goes'; chapter is abbreviated as C.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbiting is British slang for talking on and on, which is exactly what idle prattling or gabbling is.

clue.text: Tracks made by pile-up with top fully down

indicators.note: in a down clue the top letter is sent right down to the bottom, so the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: a shunt is British slang for a collision of vehicles, a pile-up

explanation.surface: Railway lines left behind after a crash, with the convertible's roof folded down.
explanation.walkthrough: SHUNT is British slang for a car crash; 'with top fully down' moves its S to the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To track an animal or person is to pursue or search for them, the verb sense of chase down.

clue.text: Many desert, led by you in the past

indicators.note: led by puts the old word for you in front of the desert word

parts.note: thou is the archaic word for you
a desert is made of sands

explanation.surface: Many people abandon things, guided by how you used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a verb (abandon) but is the noun: a desert's sands.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousands is used loosely for a very large number, i.e. a great many.

clue.text: Power lies in sexiness or refined looks

indicators.note: lies in says the power letter sits inside the rest of the wordplay
refined means processed or worked over, so the letters of sexiness or are recast

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Power, it is said, resides either in sex appeal or in sophisticated appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' looks like an adjective describing looks but it reworks SEXINESS OR, with P from 'Power' set inside by 'lies in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial expressions are looks: a look of surprise, a look of disdain.

clue.text: International tempo raised to support cold part of planet

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: C is cold, as marked on taps

indicators.note: raised means turned upward, so in a down clue the word for tempo reads from the bottom up

parts.note: tempo is pace, the speed of something

explanation.surface: An international pace raised to boost a chilly bit of the globe, like a climate summit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'raised' reads upward and 'to support' puts that piece beneath the I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A polar ice sheet covers the top or bottom of a planet, part of its surface.

clue.text: Gobbling venison up, guy that's heartless and …?

definitions.text: Gobbling venison up, guy that's heartless and …?

indicators.note: gobbling means swallowing, so the outer letters take in the other piece
heartless says the middle of guy is removed, leaving its outside letters
up in a down clue says the word for venison reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: venison is the meat of deer

explanation.surface: A man wolfing down venison is called heartless and something else: the reader fills the gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the deer word upward in this down light; 'that's heartless' empties guy. The whole clue also describes a glutton, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gobbling venison who is heartless as well fits a description of a selfish glutton: avaricious and voracious.

clue.text: Upper-class idlers, retiring, occasionally exercised

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters picked from idlers are read backwards
occasionally says only every other letter of idlers is taken

explanation.surface: Posh layabouts who withdraw from life only take exercise now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' keeps D, E, S from idlers and 'retiring' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: To have exercised a right or power is to have employed it, made use of it.

clue.text: Compile 'ten' roughly like this clu

indicators.note: roughly means approximately or carelessly, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to put together 'ten' approximately, illustrated by a clue missing its last letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition shows itself: 'clu' is a clue lacking its final E, so it is the thing it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A word cut off before its end, like the truncated clu, is unfinished or lacking a part.

clue.text: Small building suffers, having no entry places for pets

parts.note: a hut is a small simple building

indicators.note: having no entry means the first letter, the way in, is dropped

parts.note: aches means suffers pain

explanation.surface: A small shed is in a bad way, lacking a door, as a home for animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no entry' strips the first letter from ACHES, leaving CHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbits and guinea pigs are kept in wooden pens with wire fronts, their homes.

clue.text: Principal problem is to crush rise of alien resistance

indicators.note: to crush means to squeeze something within, so the problem holds the alien inside

parts.note: a headache is a problem or nuisance

indicators.note: rise of in a down clue says the word for alien reads from the bottom up

parts.note: ET is the film alien, the extraterrestrial
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: The main difficulty is how to stamp out a growing extraterrestrial resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' is a school head (the noun), not 'main'. 'rise of' reads the alien upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's principal is the person in charge of it, the head of staff.

clue.text: 'Waiter and cook' advert's about right

parts.note: to stew is to cook slowly

indicators.note: about means around, so the advert letters surround the right

parts.note: ad is short for advert; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A recruitment advert asking for a waiter and cook seems about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' is the verb STEW; the 's of advert's just says 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward serves passengers on a ship or aircraft, or attends at a club, much as a waiter does.

clue.text: We usually leave them pounds heavier and pounds lighter

definitions.text: We usually leave them pounds heavier and pounds lighter

parts.words: We usually leave them pounds heavier and pounds lighter
parts.note: after a meal out we weigh more pounds and our wallets have fewer pounds sterling

explanation.walkthrough: The two 'pounds' differ: weight gained, money spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where you pay to eat a meal leave you both fuller and poorer.

clue.text: Answer included in new collection of corniest answers

indicators.note: included in says the answer letter is put inside
a new collection of suggests the letters of corniest regathered in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A quiz compiler adds one more answer to a fresh anthology of the cheesiest replies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new collection of' rearranges CORNIEST to RECTIONS, and A goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reactions are responses to something, as answers are responses to questions.

clue.text: Chant, ingesting acid and turning on

indicators.note: ingesting means swallowing, so the singing word takes in the other

parts.note: to chant is to sing
tart means sharp or acidic in taste

explanation.surface: A 1960s scene: chanting, dropping LSD, and getting turned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acid' is not the drug but the adjective for sour: TART.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting an engine or machine is switching it on, getting it going.

clue.text: Forward on loan?

definitions.meaning: forward as in progressive, ahead of its time, developed
money paid out ahead of time, such as a sum lent against wages

explanation.definitionFit: Forward thinking is progressive or developed, and money paid ahead as a loan has been lent up front.

clue.text: Euphoric bore

definitions.meaning: euphoric means carried away with delight, enraptured
bore as the past tense of bear: carried

explanation.definitionFit: A person in rapture is carried away with joy, and goods carried from place to place have been conveyed.

clue.text: Wrong goal overturned — that's sport

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue says the combined pieces read from the bottom up

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
the goal is the net

explanation.surface: A referee's wrong decision on a goal is reversed: that's sport for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses SIN + NET as one run, giving TEN NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket game played over a net, Wimbledon's game, is a sport.

clue.text: Oldster entering northbound metro in Essen

indicators.note: northbound says the hidden letters are read backwards
entering says the answer goes into the words that follow, sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An old person boarding the underground train in the German city of Essen, heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'entering' in the definition, but it signals the hidden word; 'Oldster' alone defines. 'northbound' in a down light reads the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An older person is a senior citizen, or senior for short.

clue.text: Polished section of gate-leg antique

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A buffed piece of an old gate-leg table, the kind with folding leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished manners or style are refined and graceful.

clue.text: Country tune backing American gets into at first

indicators.note: first says this assembled piece comes before the tune
gets into says the American letters go inside the word at
backing means going backwards, so the word for tune is reversed

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A country song with an American backing track gets going at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the tune word; 'first' puts the at-with-US piece before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A central European nation with Vienna as its capital is a country.

clue.text: Article's enclosed for protective cover

indicators.note: enclosed says the article has something put inside it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article; the 's stands for has
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: An article has been wrapped up in protective packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment worn over clothes in the kitchen protects them from spills and stains.

clue.text: Ignore bush that's aggravated local residents

indicators.note: aggravated means made worse or provoked, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Letting the hedge grow wild has annoyed the people living nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The people who live next door or close by are the ones next to you.

clue.text: Metal hip with variable carbon coating

indicators.note: coating says the other letters cover the word for hip on either side

parts.note: Z is a common algebraic variable
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
in means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: A trendy metal with a carbon coating of varying thickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coating' wraps Z and C round IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluish-white chemical element used to galvanise steel is a metal.

clue.text: Remarkable Parisian on piano, soaring

parts.note: sur is French for on
P is piano, quiet, in music
rising means going up, soaring

explanation.surface: A remarkable Parisian pianist whose playing takes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' says take the French word for 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable is unexpected and astonishing.

clue.text: Getting on in prison having got caught out

indicators.note: out says the caught letter is taken away

parts.note: caged means locked up, in prison
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An elderly convict is in jail, having been caught and now released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught out' sounds like cricket, but 'out' removes the C from CAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on in years is old, advanced in age.
